builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Closed-loop evaluation of LLM agents for embedded software development
summary: The benchmark replaces one-shot synthesis and offline-correctness evaluation of embedded coding agents with closed-loop tasks in which agents build, run, and repair simulated ESP32 firmware under four feedback scenarios. It costs the effort of standing up the simulated ESP32 environment and running multi-repetition agent evaluations, plus API or local inference spend per run. It can fail to transfer because results on five simulated control tasks may not predict agent performance on real hardware, proprietary toolchains, or larger firmware codebases.
rationale: For a constrained-infrastructure engineer selecting models for embedded agent workflows, the finding that a 27B local model is viable while smaller local models degrade sharply is directly actionable, but the benchmark's five-task, simulation-only scope requires validation against the reader's actual workload before driving procurement or deployment decisions.
technique: Closed-loop benchmark for embedded coding agents

It costs the effort of standing up the simulated ESP32 environment and running multi-repetition agent evaluations, plus API or local inference spend per run. It can fail to transfer because results on five simulated control tasks may not predict agent performance on real hardware, proprietary toolchains, or larger firmware codebases.

gpt-5.4 achieves the highest pass rate among evaluated configurations without saturating the benchmark; qwen3.5-27B is the strongest observed local model; smaller local models degrade sharply in pass rate and search efficiency.
